{{nihongo|'''Odai Agata Shrine'''|小田井縣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tajima Province]].

{{wikidata link|Q21655259|ja|小田井縣神社|grok=none|check_date=2026-06-05}}

'''Odai Agata Shrine''' (おだいあがたじんじゃ) is a shrine in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|Q696388|qid=Q696388}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Hyogo|af|Hyogo-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Hyogo|ar|هيوغو (محافظة)|az|Hyoqo prefekturası|azb|هیوقو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Hyōgo|be|Хіёга|bg|Хього|bn|হিয়োগো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Hyōgo|cdo|Hyōgo-gâing|ce|Хёго (префектура)|ceb|Hyōgo-ken|ckb|پارێزگای ھیۆگۆ|cs|Prefektura Hjógo|cy|Hyōgo (talaith)|da|Hyōgo-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Hyōgo|eo|Gubernio Hiogo|es|Prefectura de Hyōgo|et|Hyōgo prefektuur|eu|Hyōgo (prefektura)|fa|استان هیوگو|fi|Hyōgon prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Hyōgo|frr|Hyōgo (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Hyōgo|gl|Prefectura de Hyōgo|hak|Hyōgo-yen|he|היוגו (מחוז)|hr|Hyōgo (prefektura)|hu|Hjógo prefektúra|hy|Հյոգո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Hyōgo|ilo|Prepektura ti Hyōgo|is|Hyogo-hérað|it|Prefettura di Hyōgo|ja|兵庫県|jv|Préfèktur Hyogo|ka|ჰიოგოს პრეფექტურა|ko|효고현|la|Hyogoensis|lg|Hyōgo Prefecture|lt|Hiogo prefektūra|lv|Hjogo prefektūra|mk|Хјого (префектура)|mni|ꯍ꯭ꯌꯣꯒꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|ह्योगो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Hyōgo|ne|ह्योगो|nl|Hyogo (prefectuur)|no|Hyōgo (prefektur)|nov|Hyōgo Prefekture|os|Хиого|pam|Prepektura ning Hyōgo|pl|Prefektura Hyōgo|pnb|ضلع ہیوگو|pt|Hyogo|ro|Prefectura Hyōgo|ru|Хиого|se|Hyōgo prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Hyōgo|si|හ්‍යෝගෝ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Hyōgo Prefecture|sk|Hjógo (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Hjogo|sr|Префектура Хјого|su|Préféktur Hyogo|sv|Hyōgo prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Hyogo|tg|Префектураи Ҳёго|th|จังหวัดเฮียวโงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Hyōgo|tr|Hyōgo|tt|Хёго (префектура)|uk|Префектура Хіого|ur|ہیوگو پریفیکچر|vi|Hyōgo|war|Hyōgo (prefektura)|wuu|兵库县|zh|兵库县|zh_classical|兵庫縣|zh_min_nan|Hyôgo-koān|zh_yue|兵庫縣|qid=Q130290}}. A subordinate shrine of Odai Agata Shrine, "Yanaginomiya Shrine," is associated with the "Toyooka Yanagi Festival," held every year on August 1 and 2. It is the largest festival in the central urban area of Toyooka. It is regarded as one of the five shrines of Tajima.

=== Enshrined deity ===
{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kunitsukuri Onamuchi-no-Mikoto}}
''Kokushi Monjo / Tajima Jinja Keifuden'' records three seats: upper seat Kunitsukuri Onamuchi-no-Mikoto, middle seat Amateru-kuni-teruhiko Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto, lower seat Watatsumi deity.

=== History ===
In ''Kokushi Monjo / Tajima Kojiki'' (Vol. 4, Kinosaki District traditions) and ''Kokushi Monjo / Tajima Jinja Keifu Denki'' (Vol. 4, Kinosaki District shrine genealogy), the following tradition appears:
{{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411}} went west into Tajima and stayed at Suganomiya. He descended to Toyooka plain and opened sacred rice fields. He also ordered Tarui Ame-Mononobe-no-Mikoto to dig a sacred spring at Kinosaki and irrigate the fields, producing auspicious rice. Therefore the land was called Toyooka-hara, and the sacred well was called Oda-i (sacred paddy well), later becoming Odai; this is why the district was called Odai Agata.

In the 3rd year, autumn, month 8 of Emperor Jinmu, Kunitsukuri Onamuchi-no-Mikoto was enshrined on a hill at Kinosaki. In month 9 of the same year, Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto was also enshrined on the same hill, and Homae-itsukinushi-no-Mikoto served before the food offerings. In regency year 3 of Empress Jingu, for merit in the Korean campaign, shrine buildings were constructed, offerings dedicated, and rites performed. The Agata governor of Kinosaki, Takemimono-no-Mikoto, served as envoy of offerings and enshrined the Great Watatsumi deities (Sokotsu, Nakatsu, and Uwatsu) in the lower seat.

In Hakuhō 3 of Emperor Tenmu (summer, month 6), when a great drought struck the realm, rain was prayed for at Odai Agata Shrine, ritual implements were placed in the shrine storehouse, and for the first time the Hokotate rite and Mitoage rite were performed; later these came to be called "Hokotate Shinji" and "Kawachi Shinji."

Also, the sacred sake place was ritually established, sake was brewed, food deities were worshipped, food offerings were prepared and presented. The Sakatare deity ({{ill|Sakatare Shrine|Q11644306|qid=Q11644306}}) and Miketsu deity in Minie village (present Mie) are identified with these. The Kinosaki district governor Mononobe Karakuni no Muraji Kugui presided over this.

=== Site information ===
; Access
''On foot''
* From {{ill|Toyooka Station (Hyōgo)|Q871612|qid=Q871612|lt=Toyooka Station}} (JR West San'in Main Line), 1,400 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}} east-northeast
* From {{ill|Kōnotori-no-sato Station|Q7676863|qid=Q7676863}} (Kyoto Tango Railway Miyatoyo Line), 1,500 meters west-southwest

''By car''
* Head toward Toyooka and go north along National Route 312 by the Maruyama River; at the north edge of the urban area, below the west side of the road at the Horikawa-bashi signal. No parking lot.
